messages:
sam: Heads-up — we're proposing a small-but-impactful change to how routing keys are represented in console telemetry. Current column is `route_id` (int); we want a stable `route_key` (string) that survives route renames and cross-tenant aliasing. Thoughts on compatibility approach?

anika: +1 on stable string keys. Can we avoid a full schema rename by adding `route_key` as a nullable column and backfill progressively? avoids big downtime.

liam: Backfill plan sounds good. We need to consider queries used by dashboards: some agg queries join on route_id currently. If we add route_key we should add an indexed functional index to cover most queries.

rafa: For joins: I suggest a migration pattern w/ a DB view that exposes `route_key` via COALESCE(route_key, route_lookup(route_id)) and then rewrite internal queries to read from the view first. That buys time to backfill and roll out.

sam: Nice idea. Implementation details? route_lookup() would be a lookup to the route catalog service; calling external service from query is no-go. Need the mapping in DB (small table) or a cached column.

anika: Agree — keep mapping in DB. We can create `routes_v1` mapping table (route_id -> route_key, tenant_id) and populate during deployment. Then view can join to that table.

liam: We also need to think about quota accounting. Quotas are currently keyed by route_id; if we switch to route_key we must maintain 1:1 mapping during transition. Otherwise quota billing graphs will be inconsistent.

rafa: Quota bridge: write-through on updates. At write time, middleware should write both route_id and route_key atomically (two columns in same tx). Reads for quota aggregation use COALESCE(route_key, inferred_key). We'll add a feature flag to opt-in.

tara: UX note: Console rollouts must show both legacy id and new key until rollout is fully complete. Dashboard filters need to accept either id or key. Otherwise support tickets will blow up.

sam: Good point. We'll add a transient mapping layer in the console that translates user-entered identifiers and shows deprecation hint.

anika: Backfill script sketch:
```sql
-- populate route_key for recent telemetry rows
UPDATE telemetry_events t
SET route_key = r.route_key
FROM routes_v1 r
WHERE t.route_id = r.route_id
  AND t.route_key IS NULL
  AND t.created_at > now() - interval '30 days';
```
We'll run incremental windows sorted by created_at to avoid long table locks.

liam: Make sure to create `route_key` with same collation and a small varchar length (e.g., varchar(128)). Add an index on (tenant_id, route_key, created_at) partial for alive rows.

rafa: Can we avoid immediate reindexing of huge tables? Suggest using partial indexes + nightly batch to backfill hot partitions first.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Migration `add-route_key-v1` created. Will run in dry mode on staging at 2026-04-02T03:00Z.

sam: After staging dry run, we'll do canary on low-traffic shard for two days, monitor dashboard query latencies and quota deltas. If safe, promote to wider fleet.

anika: Rollout UX: add a console banner that says "Route identifier migration in progress — you can use both route id and route key" with a link to docs. Also provide a query translator tool in debug console.

liam: API compatibility: keep internal endpoints accepting route_id param, but add `route_key` query param support. If both supplied, validate they map to same route. If mismatch, return 400 with helpful message.

rafa: Tests: unit for mapping logic, e2e for console filters (id & key), and a retro test that ensures quotas before/after align within a small epsilon.

tara: Ops: create a short runbook for support to map legacy tickets that reference route ids to route keys (one-liner SQL).

sam: Ok action items: 1) anika create migration PR with view + partial index + backfill script; 2) liam update query layer to read from view and accept route_key; 3) rafa implement write-through in middleware and feature flag; 4) tara draft console banner + docs; 5) infra-bot schedule staging dry run.

anika: I'll start the PR tonight and tag reviewers. Will include metrics we should collect during canary.

liam: I'll add compatibility checks to the query planner and smoke tests.

rafa: I'll wire the write-through flagged behind `route_key_migration` and emit a delta metric we can alert on.

tara: I'll prepare the console copy and support runbook.

sam: Thanks team. Keep thread updated with staging run results and any unexpected edge cases. :thumbsup:
